questions.q: If content matches the conditions of more than one sensitivity label, which label is applied?
options: The label with the highest priority number in the ranked list
The label that was created most recently
The label with the shortest name
All matching labels are applied at once
questions.explain: A single item can carry only one label, so Microsoft Purview resolves conflicts by priority order: the highest-priority matching label wins.

questions.q: What do auto-labeling policies use to decide when to recommend or apply a label?
options: Sensitive information types, such as credit card numbers, SSNs, or passport numbers detected in the content
The file's creation date only
A random sample of content chosen weekly
The user's job title in Microsoft Entra ID
questions.explain: Auto-labeling conditions are built on sensitive information types — the same detection catalog used for data loss prevention — so matching content can be labeled with no manual choice.

questions.q: What must a Fabric tenant admin turn on before sensitivity labels work on Fabric and Power BI content at all?
options: The tenant setting "Allow users to apply sensitivity labels for Power BI content"
Row-level security on every semantic model
The Fabric capacity's autoscale option
Git integration for every workspace
questions.explain: Sensitivity labels don't appear in Fabric at all until this tenant setting is explicitly enabled in the Fabric admin portal.

questions.q: What's the difference between a label's protection actions and classification-only labeling?
options: Protection actions (encryption, content marking, access restrictions) technically enforce something; classification-only labels just tag content for reporting with no enforcement
Protection actions only apply to email, never to files or Fabric items
Classification-only labels can never be seen by end users
There is no difference — every sensitivity label enforces the same restrictions
questions.explain: Some labels exist purely to classify content for governance and reporting; others additionally carry protection actions like encryption, watermarking, or sharing restrictions.

questions.q: Where does an admin go to see how sensitivity labels are actually being applied across the whole tenant?
options: The Microsoft Purview compliance portal's data classification and label analytics reporting
The Fabric capacity metrics app
The individual label's Edit label screen
The Power BI Desktop file properties dialog
questions.explain: Data classification reporting in the Purview compliance portal gives a tenant-wide view of label coverage, separate from any single label or policy configuration screen.
